summary: This program stores seven facts about a giraffe in variables, each using the data type that fits the fact, then prints them all as a tidy list of labelled lines.

lines.text:
Text goes in quotes, making this a string 
ever treated as a word rather than a number.
A measurement with a fractional part needs a float; the variable name records the unit so the number is never ambiguous.
A yes-or-no fact is a Boolean, and Python spells its two values `True` and `False` with a capital letter — lowercase `false` would be an error.
Whole counts like speed, spots, and years are integers; there is no need for a decimal point when nothing is ever half a spot.
The `f` before the quote lets each `{variable}` be swapped for its value, and each `\n` starts a new line, so one print statement produces Samantha's whole notebook page.
